Hi! If I may, I wanna throwback to the last @itsloungesessions for a minute. 

See, I was still very much in the grey area at this point with my right hip injury (if you’re just finding out - I’ll be ok! Just a bunch of PT in the future!) and I was very unsure if I’d be able to make it at all, let alone for the full 6 hours our B4B set.

Well, I lasted 3 before my left leg was screaming from having all the extra weight on it and I had to go. Serious shout outs to @itsanthonyromano (for making sure I had a stool in the booth - swipe to the last slide) and to @leftimusic & @josie.musique for just being great all around and picking up the slack for me in my moment of need. 🙏🏻

And if I’m being honest - that’s what I love about the Lounge Sessions crew. Everyone’s there for the right reasons. The music and the community. It feels safe and full of joy and reminds me why I got into this in the first place. ❤️

That being said it was a sick party and one of my favorite ones yet and I wanted it on the timeline. Thanks to everyone who contributed to this carousel. Much love to y’all. 🫶🏻

Vol.4 - we have an incredible lineup featuring four talented artists, two debuts who will guide us through an exhilarating journey of sound and rhythm.

First up, we are thrilled to introduce @orrador Hailing from Georgia and now based in Brooklyn, Niko and Bakuri explore a range of techno styles—from groovy, hypnotic minimalism to driving, atmospheric forms. Their debut EP, 107, released this November, showcases their focus on clear, rhythmic detail. 

Next, we welcome back @firebunny 
Firebunny is recognized for her high-energy hard techno sounds, and her genre-blending ability makes her performances unique and engaging for a wide range of electronic music fans. However, on this special night, she will present a distinctive techno set that fuses driving basslines with dark, groovy industrial and trance elements. Expect to experience a touch of her sensuality woven throughout the soundscape.

Following her will be another debut @andre.ballalai Originally from Brazil, he has over 20 years behind the decks, DJ Andre-KX is a seasoned force in the techno scene. Known for his high-energy sets, he merges the classic craft of vinyl turntablism and scratching with fast CDJ tricks, creating an electrifying blend of old-school technique and the uprising NY Techno spirit. His dynamic sets are infused with the raw beats of drum and bass, the grit of electro, and the groove of funky techno, keeping dance floors alive and moving.

And finally, we have the ever-magnetic @PFDA A familiar face and one of our favorites, he will be bringing back his fiery closing set that you simply cannot miss. Get ready for an unforgettable end to the night! 🔥

Dec 2001 → Dec 2025 ✨
How it started vs how it’s going.

This was me outside Macy’s at Christmas in 2001, after dancing all night at ARC (formerly Vinyl) in NYC to Danny Tenaglia. No plan. No roadmap. Just love for the music, and a deep sense that it truly mattered to me..

Fast forward 24 years — I’ve played New York countless times, and tonight I hosted my first-ever sold out workshop here, followed by a show at SILO, one of the hottest rooms in the city.

In the first photo, I knew nothing.
In the second, I know a lot — and I’m still learning.

What I’m most grateful for is getting to share what I’ve learned with artists who look just like I did in that first photo: curious, hopeful, and hungry to find their place.

Thank you to everyone who sent love and condolences over the last 24 hours. It’s been heavy, but being in New York tonight — surrounded by friends and music — gave me a few minutes of light, and I’m deeply grateful for that. 🖤

Thank you @shutupanddance for sharing this memory!

RUSH kicks off 2026 with a bang: Héctor Oaks headlines alongside Estella Boersma, BAUGRUPPE90 and Vilë on February 13.

The Spanish powerhouse made his mark at the first-ever edition of RUSH in 2023, turning the room on its head with a blindingly intense, high velocity all-vinyl set. He makes his long awaited return to the Main Hall alongside Dutch raver sorceress Estella Boersma and Berlin’s beloved duo BAUGRUPPE90. Colombian-born, NY-based artist Vilë completes the lineup, making her RUSH debut.

Tickets on sale now via link in bio

(2/6) In 2025, @outlinefest reached new heights, with four stellar editions culminating in a sold-out fifth anniversary show to close out the year. 

Across each of the installations, the series represented about as wide a breadth as you can ask for:

Back-to-back shows in the spring spanned five decades of psychedelic rock with headlining sets from Michael Rother, Thurston Moore in March and Explosions in the Sky and múm in April. The moment when Moore joined Rother onstage for an extended jam stands as a high point for the series. 

Summer’s edition went hard on searing hyperpop, avant-garde hip-hop, leftfield club fusions and more. Stretching out across the venue, with performances in the Main Hall and Ruins, Jockstrap, Kenny Mason, Jane Remover and more met the moment with a blistering night of edgy catharsis.

Then to wrap the year, the series pulled a 180 and went deep into Scandinavian downtempo. October’s closing edition led with the enveloping pop of Erika de Casier and her art-school pop contemporaries Smerz, alongside a lineup of like-minded artists whose work exemplifies an impossibly alluring neo-retro cool. It was a sublime wrap to OUTLINE’s biggest year to date. 

A huge thanks to almost 100 artists who’ve played OUTLINE shows to date. Five years is just the beginning.

For the opening, I made a medicinal soup of silkie chicken and shen ling bai zhu san, an ancient blend of herbs formulated to support with Qi depletion in the lung-spleen axis where we hold and process grief. This was paired with a guided meditation on death as transformation—decomposition, regeneration, ancestral reunion, and return to nature. In slowing down through this ritual, we are reminded that mortality gives life meaning, and that endings are portals to new forms of becoming.

Thanks to @jonopandolfi for lending the bowls, @architecture.research.office @tangible.space for lending the stools, @hatnimlee for the photos, and @linyee_is_outside @john__grund for the invitation to be a part of this beautiful show 🤍

Read My Phone, The Moon at @craftandrelease on Monday.  A piece about using social media during heartbreak. Gonna share a snippet here-

“It’s been said in movies, novels, and romantic tales that we all look up at the same moon, an expression to exemplify that distance could never end one’s love. I once found this idea trite, but now it may have been so—except the moon is man made and handheld, accessible 24 hours a day, and affecting the cycles of our lives. 

The space that existed prior to our technological advancements is no longer. I didn’t contact him in hopes of understanding the ending of our relationship. Why would I? It was all right there. I could see his face, read his captions, and mold him into the person I was falling in love with or someone I completely despised. 

Obsessing over the ending of our relationship became my North Star. It wasn’t the sky that lit up my face, it was light that cascaded from my phone. I didn’t pray to the stars. I refreshed my timeline. I tapped my screen in the middle of conversations. I woke up at 2 am, 4 am, and 6 to see if he’d decided to come back to me.”

Grateful for the opportunity to tell a story I have revisited time and time again to an audience that was so willing to hear me out. Photos by @laquanndawson. Thank you to @bedstuybrat and @nnekaj for letting me participate in their evening.

Koju (@sushikoju) at the Ace Hotel Brooklyn is the kind of omakase that immediately puts you at ease. Sushi counters oftentimes can feel formal or intimidating, but Executive Chef Kevin Garrison has an effortless, cool energy that makes the whole experience feel welcoming. You can tell he is deeply trained, but he doesn’t make a show of it. His confidence comes through in the food, not the attitude.

The 14-course tasting menu ($145) was thoughtfully paced and just right in portions. Everything felt clean, seasonal, and intentional without trying too hard. High-quality fish, beautifully handled rice, and warm bites served at the perfect moment made the whole meal feel quietly refined. For the experience, quality, and the location, the price feels fair.

The drink list is equally strong, with a great selection of sake and cocktails that pair naturally with the progression of courses. Nothing overly flashy, simply well chosen and well balanced.

What really stayed with me was the atmosphere. Chef Kevin creates a counter experience that feels relaxed and genuinely fun, almost like sitting with someone who loves what they do and wants you to enjoy it too. It is refreshing to have an omakase that takes the food seriously without taking itself too seriously.

“Dig a Hole… a Nest” — a group show on view Dec 4–Jan 31 at @acehotelbrooklyn, brought together by the best @fieldmeridians.
I’ll be showing work among a community of fellow artists and land workers as we hold space for this season of decay, rest, and transformation.
✨Join us for opening gathering tomorrow 12/4, 7–9pm.

I’ll be sharing three altars—odes to the intimacy and kinship formed with three plants over this past farm season: Rue, Chamomile, and Mugwort. While in full bloom, each plant was prepared as a flower essence, its energetic imprint held in water, allowing the relationship to persist in another form.
Each altar invites quiet connection and reverence through three states of the plant’s time:
the essence (its memory), the seeds (its future), and the plant in decay (its present).
Visitors are welcome to engage with the essences and create their own moment of communion with each plant.

THURSDAY, 7-9PM! Join us at the @acehotelbrooklyn for the opening of 𝓓𝓲𝓰 𝓪 𝓱𝓸𝓵𝓮...𝓐 𝓷𝓮𝓼𝓽, a show curated by Field Meridians to explore winter as a season of rest and transformation. We’ve invited artists who also tend soil and seas to gather their works around a table and honor soil as master composter, hole, planetary membrane, gravesite and nest.

Honcho returns to Signal for our last Sunday session of 2025, featuring two favorites. The acid house legend, Miami’s Mystic Bill, and one of the freshest talents we’ve had the pleasure to get to know these past few years: maenad. 

NOTE: We’re pushing the party a little earlier to capture more of the afternoon sun and sunset hours – 1pm-10pm this time, kicking off right as Faggots are Women wraps up.. 

MYSTIC BILL
A member of Chicago’s second wave of house – known for raw, tracky, acid-driven sets. Cutting his teeth in late-’80s/early-’90s Chicago, he played rooms like Shelter, Smarbar and Crobar, holding residencies alongside Ralphie Rosario, Derrick Carter & Mark Farina. He later returned home to Miami to hold residencies at Electric Pickle and Gramps.

As a producer and selector, Bill’s imprint runs through pillars like Trax, Relief, Classic Music Company, Strictly Rhythm, Snuff Trax, and Chi-Wax—while also exploring darker EBM/industrial terrain under his Savage Hymn alias on Dark Entries.

MAENAD
A musician and multimedia artist now based in Brooklyn, but someone we got to know deeply in Pittsburgh. Training originally as a classical singer, she found a home in Pittsburgh’s queer club scene where the strong sense of community and love inspired her to infuse her djing with emotional vocal tracks and warm sentimental sounds. She seeks constantly to share euphoria found only on the dance floor and to uplift and celebrate trans people. If you don’t know maenad yet, it’s time to change that. She is pure joy.

December 8 was an incredible night, one I’m still processing a week later.

We sold a bunch of tickets and played nearly two hours of music. I’m so grateful to everyone who came out. Friends, family, familiar faces, and people I’d never met before. Folks I hadn’t seen in a long time made the effort to show up, and that meant more than I can say.

Huge gratitude to my bandmates. This night doesn’t happen without them.

I almost canceled this show.

Looking back, I’m so proud I stayed the course. In 2025, I played two major shows at Nublu, a venue I’ve always wanted to play, with a band that feels incredibly alive. June 23 felt grounded and expansive. December 8 was high energy, uncertain, and emotionally charged. I was playing through nerves, but those nerves gave way to moments of surrender and real magic. Both nights felt spiritual.

I’m proud of staying true to my vision through all of it. The wins, the stress, the doubt, the joy.

As I head into the new year, I’m feeling called to slow down and return to writing.

So much gratitude for this year, this community, and this music. 💛

Legendary Chris Rob brings Jazz in Space to Dead Letter No. 9 ✨ 
🚨🚨🚨🚨 Hey NYC come out to an evening where jazz, soul, and groove move freely and the music unfolds in real time.

Amazingly talented virtuoso musician ranging from keyboardist, pianist, composer, vocalist, and musical director, Chris Rob moves effortlessly across jazz, R&B, soul, funk, and hip-hop, leading with intuition, deep pocket, and musical intelligence.

He has brought his musical excellence to other legends Stevie Wonder, Roberta Flack, Nile Rodgers, Anita Baker, Kool & the Gang, and hip-hop legends Rakim, Talib Kweli, CL Smooth, Warren G, and Slum Village, and served as music director for John Legend’s Get Lifted Tour.

Beyond the stage, Chris Rob currently composes for Netflix’s 

The Upshaws and recently scored the acclaimed documentary Outstanding: A Comedy Revolution. His work has also been featured in McDonald’s “Black & Positively Golden” campaign and Tyler Perry’s Peeples. 🙌🏾🙌🏾🙌🏾🙌🏾 One of Chicago’s and Midwest’s finest…

deep reverence for our autumn PMS co-hosts: three floral symbols of the madonna.  
  
SEPTEMBER | MARIGOLD : In Mexico, they guide spirits during Día de los Muertos; in South Asia, they’re used in temple offerings; in Europe, “Mary’s Gold” flowers are offered to the Virgin Mary in place of coins. Marigolds are natural insect repellers while attracting pollinators, so farmers often plant marigolds to protect other crops. Marigolds are used as natural dyes and in chicken feed to make egg yolks more vibrant… there’s no part of the food pyramid this diva doesn’t touch! Marigolds are used in ointments for wounds, burns, & rashes; they offer anti-inflammatory & anti-microbial benefits. Calendula marigolds help digestion &… wait for it… menstrual regulation!  
  
OCTOBER | WHITE ROSE : Roses have anti-inflammatory & mild antiseptic properties, & are used in perfumery, cuisine, and traditional medicine.  They have an “aromatic architecture”: perfumers describe rose scents as olfactory chords (like musical chords) with distinct head, heart, & base notes. White roses symbolize purity, innocence, and spiritual love— which is why they are often depicted beside the Virgin Mary, or in the hand of The Fool in Tarot as he takes a faithful, optimistic leap into the unknown (which is why @maxstossel & I love this flower so much).  
  
NOVEMBER | CALLA LILY : what we see is not the calla lily’s true flower, but a spathe: a modified leaf that wraps around a central spadix, where the plant’s actual tiny flowers cluster. Because of its unisexual floral structure, the calla lily is often interpreted as a symbol of unity beyond binaries & of harmony between opposites. We love a non-binary queen! Calla lilies have a history of rich cultural symbolism, particularly around the divine feminine and the figure of Mother (often connected to the Virgin Mary due to its chalice shape). According to Greek myth, calla (from the Greek “kallos” or beauty) was created from Hera’s spilled milk, linking it to divine motherhood and creation.

Son of legendary funk guitarist / composer / arranger DENNIS “ MENACE “ WEEDEN [credits: France Joli, Taana Gardner, Secret Weapon, Gwen McRae, and more] grandson of Terry Pollard [Detroit Rock & Roll Hall of fame and American jazz legend]

Stopped by @massaranyc, @rezdoranyc’s sister restaurant, last week and honestly… it hit the spot. We got the paccheri pomodoro pasta, two candele (ragu bolognese) and a baby gem salad.

➡️ Pomodoro 🍝— 8/10
Classic, simple, comforting. The sauce was bright and flavorful and I couldn’t stop eating it, but the presentation (and portion size) wasn’t great - it just looked like it was plopped on the plate. However, I would still order it again!

➡️ Candele Ragu Pasta 🍝— 8/10
This one was it. Rich, savory, and the pasta was perfectly al dente. Cozy, satisfying, and definitely the star of the meal.

➡️ Baby Gem 🥗— 7/10
The salad was fresh and crisp. Would order again!

The portions were tiny but the meal was great, will definitely go back!

audio.title: Let Me Love You (feat. Justin Bieber)

caption:
While directing this interview with David Harbour back in 2018 for WHOSAY (now a subsidiary of Paramount + Advertising), promoting Stranger Things, I was really struck with how incredibly humble, likable and real this guy was. Undoubtedly, my favorite “celebrity interview” of the slew we produced that year. 
David acts because he has to. He seems to ascribe to the no choice club; it’s a survival mechanism. I really enjoy the call to action being that you do something of import in this life because you have to, not because you want to. This is a short clip of the 20 minute cut. Thunderbolts drops today. I’m going to see it.

I had the most magical trip to NY this past week…by myself. Years ago, the thought of traveling by myself in a crowded city and navigating it by myself and doing activities by myself would have paralyzed me. I never would have done a trip like this, but it ended up being one of the best trips of my life. I did all the things young Kate would have loved to do, like see the @therockettes or playing with Marvel characters at @madametussaudsusa and seeing the Christmas tree at Rockefeller. I also honored adult Kate by seeing my boyfriend, Machine Gun Kelly and bought beautiful clothing and ate good meals. And honestly, I’m a fabulous date. I like me and I am capable of doing lots of things! Highly recommend taking a trip by yourself to remember who the fuck you are. #newyork #christmas #mgk #travel #nyc

👉 在 (zài): used with places to show location

Example: 我在学校。

👉 哪里 (nǎlǐ): used in questions to ask “where**
→ Structure: Subject + 在 + 哪里？
Example: 你在哪里？
Pinyin: Nǐ zài nǎlǐ?
Meaning: Where are you?

👉这里 – zhèlǐ – noun / adverb (place word) – here

I swung by @treadwellpark and quickly realized it’s one of those places you can pull up to any time of year, but it feels extra cozy right now with the holiday spirit. ✨🎄.
Both the Downtown and Uptown spots have this easy, come-as-you-are vibe that makes hanging out feel fun. 🍻😌.
Big bar, roomy tables, and a crowd that’s there to actually enjoy themselves without making it a whole thing. 🪩🙌. Bring friends or go solo, either way you settle in fast. 🤗🧥.The food hit the spot too. 🥗🔥.
From their classic wings, to their Giant Soft Pretzel, with all the dips, the place is basically the table-share that everyone enjoys 🥨✔️.
And if you’re into sandwiches, the “Sweet & Spicy” Crispy Chicken Sandwich is one of those things you order once and automatically plan to order again. 🍗🔥.But if what you want is a drink, tear no more, there are over 20 beers on tap, plus cider, wine, and cocktails if you want to mix it up. 🍺🍷🍹.
Screens for games (and special nights like @dancingwiththestars watching parties), ping-pong, pinball, or you can just hang and keep things low-key. 🏓🎯.
It’s the kind of spot that works for whatever mood you’re in. 🎁❄️.If it’s been on your radar (Or this is the first time you heard about it), consider this your sign to go. 🦄🌈 #AColoROYMoment

Brat behavior discourse of the week 

@puptosa is publicly accusing his handler @themazrim of skipping his weekly bath. Odin is away so this is advanced, extra-credit brattiness. (It also reminds me of my pup Ruffus telling everyone I “abandon” him… even if I’m just going to the bathroom.)

What I actually love about this little social media “drama” is that it highlights two things bratty behavior gets right:

1. You don’t get to be this public, playful, and unthreatened unless the dynamic is secure. That level of teasing only works when the relationship underneath it is solid.
2. Good brats understand that you need rules in order to bend them. Brattiness lives inside a framework. You’ve gotta know the rules to break them.

It’s actually a beautiful exchange between people who care deeply for each other.

So am I on Team Tosa (give him a bath) or Team Odin (punish him)? Honestly… both. If it was me, Tosa would absolutely get a bath—but I hope he’s prepared for some very intentional submersion, intense breath work, and learning why brats don’t bite the hand that holds the leash.

caption:
This time of year can feel heavy.

Behind the smiles and celebrations, so many of us are carrying things no one sees.
Quiet decisions. Long nights. Risks taken without applause. Wins we didn’t stop to celebrate.

This photo made me think about the “packages” this year brought.
Some showed up as joy and growth.
Others arrived as lessons we didn’t ask for.
All of them asked something of us.

If you’re ending the year tired but still standing… proud but reflective… hopeful even with uncertainty—you’re not behind. You’re human.

My wish for you this season:
that you see the value of what you carried,
the impact of what you built,
and the strength it took to keep going.

Save this for when you need it and don’t forget to share it with someone who’s been holding it together

Wishing you a holiday season that brings you peace, real rest, and incredible moments that feel like a deep breath.

Happy holidays 💕

On 9/16/25 I had the pleasure of walking in Danielle‘s Leather‘s family and friends fashion show, which was held in HK Hall. It was a blast opportunity because I got to walk in not only the morning but also the afternoon show.

I had the pleasure of walking for three designers: 1. Mario Benton, @mariobpro ; 2. @tenacioussoulsclothing ; and 3. @danielsleather. It was an amazing opportunity to connect with designers and other models who came together to make it an impactful night.

I was also blessed to have run into Treach from Naughty By Nature. He was down to earth and spoke to everybody in the crowd that asked for a moment his attention.

another blessing overall. Looking forward to each and every opportunity to walk and exhibit designers creations, as well as to contribute to the causes that help guide their creation. Blessings to Daniel‘s Leather and its attention to those dealing with physical infirmities, but just as worthy of gracing the runway as all others.
You can’t do EPIC shit with basic people. A full circle moment for me going from a promo shoot to walking the runway for @cultofindividuality 💔🚶🏽📸 my heart on my sleeve for you @junikdesigner 🤞🏽

On the first snow day of the year, a day I anticipate with baited breath every year hoping something in the world around me will change when it’s filled with ice (usually it’s that we’d get a day off in school to celebrate snow day but alas childhood is over) — I set out on a voyage with @barzakh.cafe to @cafe.erzulie for the Haza Winter Souk @thehazaparty - a wonderful collaboration of musical acts and vendors. 

As a chaiwali, I had to set up way early - get my potion pots going, get that boil simmering. As vendors trickled in, everyone halted by the chai pop - “you’re going to bring all the warmth to this space, aren’t you?”, one of them said passing me by. 

If I could describe what I do for a living I’d say “I bring the vibes” and without my vibes everything is just a little less magical, a little less cinematic. I’m the sprinkled fairy dust, the scent of cinnamon and cloves you only realise you’re missing when I leave your environment ✨

We made so many friends that day! Making chai at a party can feel like being a DJ. The warmth gets people flocking. Thank you @barzakh.cafe , @cafe.erzulie and @thehazaparty for the opportunity! Special shoutout to DJ @myyuh__ 💛🙏

location.name: Le Bain at The Standard, High Line

caption:
📸 JDH & Dave P by @neilaline 

Another very special night tonight as we tap back into early-2010s Le Bain—with one of the parties that helped define the room: FIXED. Founded 20 years ago by JDH + Dave P, FIXED has been building a lane for NYC—keeping the city plugged into the wider world and bringing European artists here for their first time. A real North Star for the underground dance music we love.

JDH and Dave P are “influencers,” just not the grinchy kind—they’re scene-shapers, culture-morphers, body-movers. JDH runs probably the best club in NYC (or maybe Brooklyn? 😂) Good Room. Dave P runs probably the best indie festival in the USA, Making Time (among other things). It’s been years since they played the Le Bain skyline—and we’ve missed that.

Come up tonight @lebainnyc 🦄 It’s time to GET FIXED.
